blocks.text: Genes from a wide range of organisms can be added to plasmids and put into bacteria, and the transgenic bacteria then make large amounts of the proteins coded by the foreign genes.

blocks.caption: Uses of transgenic bacteria
rows: insulin (diabetes), clotting factors (haemophilia), hepatitis B vaccine, Covid-19 vaccine, human growth hormone (dwarfism), interferon (some cancers), erythropoietin (anaemia), tissue plasminogen activator (dissolves blood clots)
alpha-amylase (starch to simple sugars), chymosin (clots milk protein for cheese), pectin-esterase (clearer fruit juice)
enzymes that break down toxins and turn pollutants into less toxic forms
leaching copper from ore, cleaning up mercury pollution, detecting arsenic in drinking water
